chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hariz said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Fear Allah, and preserve your religion through asceticism (al-wara'), and strengthen it through piety (al-taqiyyah) and self-sufficiency from Allah by seeking one's needs from the ruler. And know that whoever humbles himself to the ruler, or to one who differs with him in religion while seeking what is in his hand from worldly goods, Allah will make him sluggish, detest him, and entrust him to himself. If he conquers something from his worldly goods, Allah will remove the blessing from him, and will not reward him for anything he spends in Hajj, or manumission, or goodness.

key_terms.أَخْمَلَهُ: He made him sluggish or lazy (in worship)
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: Piety or precaution, often implying strategic concealment or self-preservation
key_terms.الْوَرَعِ: Asceticism or piety in avoiding doubtful matters
key_terms.صَاحِبِ سُلْطَانٍ: The ruler or holder of political authority

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of seeking worldly favors from political rulers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links *al-wara'* (asceticism) and *al-taqiyya* (prudence) to political independence, warning that seeking worldly favors from rulers leads to divine abandonment (*wakalah*). This teaching underscores the Shia concept of avoiding subservience to unjust authority to preserve spiritual integrity, noting that even major acts of worship like Hajj lose their blessing if the believer's heart is attached to the ruler's worldly gifts.
